newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products weaker, gas oil slips $5.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products weaker, gas oil slips $5.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were all weaker on Tuesday, traders said.
Gasoline prices were unchanged to softer. Weaker U.S. markets had tightened transatlantic arbitrage opportunities but the market was finding some support in ongoing interest for low octane material.
The U.S. recently sucked up 1-1.5 million tonnes of regular unleaded from the Med in the first half of January, leaving the regular market looking better balanced, traders said.
They said demand for premium unleaded was weak. Prices talked in a slight softer, wider range around $214/$217 cif Med.
Naphtha held steady but high freight rates continued to hamper trade. Traders said a shift to late Feb demand provided a balance for the prompt market. Cargoes talked $216/$218 cif Med.
Gas oil slipped $5.25 a tonne in line, dragged lower by weaker NYMEX heating oil, ample U.S. supplies and warmer weather in Europe and the United States.
Volume was very thin, with increasingly expensive and scarce shipping the main culprit. Rates for cross-Mediterranean voyages were running at around Worldscale 285/290, traders said.
Russian was rumoured done at high cif quotes +$0.50 basis Genoa, around $1.50 easier.
Enquiry for low sulphur diesel remains lacklustre but attention is focussed on an Indian tender for 1.0 percent and 0.25 percent diesel for March due out on Friday.
High sulphur fuel oil fell again as prices slumped not only in NWE but also in Asian markets.
Isolated bunker demand was seen for February, but few requirements were seen for January.
Low sulphur fuel oil was weaker too, continuing the trend of the month, and offers into Italy were thought to be as low as $115.
